activation_policy.reason: Activation improves over the non-crossfit collapse but does not beat prompt+embedding on the selected F1/accuracy/recall/FPR tradeoff; full fusion only marginally improves AUROC while reducing recall/F1.

embedding_policy.reason: Prompt+embedding improved AUROC, F1, accuracy, and FPR over prompt-only in cross-fit leakage-free reviewed split stability, with a small recall tradeoff.

limitations: Reviewed rows are still adaptively selected hard cases, not a fixed deployment-distribution test set.
The selected threshold is the modal split-selected threshold, not a final deployment threshold.
External baseline results rely on benchmark-native label mappings and should be expanded to additional public guardrail benchmarks and stronger guard models.
Activation should be revisited on a blind holdout and with larger reviewed training data before assigning positive runtime weight.
rationale: The cross-fit leakage-free protocol retrains activation probes inside each split and uses out-of-fold activation predictions for calibration weight selection. Under that protocol, activation has some signal but does not improve the selected runtime tradeoff over prompt+embedding. Prompt+embedding has the best mean F1/accuracy and lower FPR than prompt-only, with a small recall tradeoff. The full prompt+embedding+activation condition has marginally higher AUROC, but lower recall/F1 and unstable activation weight selection, so activation remains an audit/research signal pending a blind holdout.

reviewed_split_stability.protocol: Each split trains a fresh activation probe on calibration rows only. Calibration activation_probability values are out-of-fold predictions inside the calibration split, and holdout values are out-of-split predictions from a probe trained on the full calibration split.
